svg.title: How create checks first and goes on where it stopped
svg.desc: python3 .github/blueprint.py create starts with its preflight, which only asks: Python, Git and the identity of the first commit, the GitHub CLI and its sign-in with the scopes repo and workflow, the owner and the name. A finding marked with ✘ stops it before anything is made and names the command that fixes it; python3 .github/blueprint.py doctor shows the same alone. A new copy then gets git init, its first commit and gh repo create with the push. A folder whose origin pushes to the repository on GitHub already, from a run that stopped midway, gets only the push when GitHub has no branch main yet. Both end with settings apply and the checklist.
